rounds.oracle: Enumerate all subsets of at most K original ids; test touching-compatible intervals independently; maximize (profit, negative cardinality) and verify chronological witness.
rounds.referenceMeasurement: Unmodified Python sys.settrace call-boundary observations at best_schedule/reconstruct/split. Count slots in distinct four-field job-record lists reachable from active candidate frames, recursively traversing pending stack containers. Aliases to the same list count once. Does not measure full peak RAM, score/work arrays, allocator overhead, or all transient allocations.
rounds.scope: Finite independent correctness cases, maximum supported-size boundary, candidate own tests and structured live-reference observations. Does not prove all-input correctness, asymptotic complexity, or whole-interview accuracy.

findings.finiteCorrectness: All three untouched listings passed the same 1998 independent subset-oracle cases, their supplied tests and the supported N=2000/K=50 boundary. The oracle checks both optimal profit and minimum cardinality, unique valid identifiers and chronological compatibility.
findings.recursiveStorage: On the supplied negative-prefix family with M negative jobs followed by K=2^d positive unit-profit jobs, the recursive listing retains distinct ancestor left lists. Measured call-boundary job-list slots equal M(d+1)+3K-2, including the retained root and pending right siblings. For M=256/K=32, 1630 slots remain live across 288 records. Deleting the child end_order variable does not release caller-owned left lists.
findings.correctedStorage: The explicit-stack listing had 288 job-list slots at observed split-call boundaries for the same family; the two-ordering listing had 576. These are job-reference measurements, not total peak RAM. Source inspection shows helpers return before child processing and caller parent aliases are removed before pushing children.
findings.complexityScope: The recursive ownership argument omits overlapping ancestor lists. Under the usual parameterized analysis, this family gives a retained-list term proportional to M log K. The listing enforces finite K<=50 and N<=2000; finite measurements do not by themselves prove an unbounded asymptotic lower bound. The explicit-stack and two-ordering corrections require their separate full work-array/partition accounting.
findings.twoOrderingWorkArgument: After two global sorts, a node of size n and capacity c performs O(nc) arithmetic operations. At each depth, child job sets are disjoint and capacities are at most ceil(C/2^d), with C=min(K,N); clamping only reduces them. Summing disjoint node sizes and the halving capacities gives O(NC) reconstruction work. This is an arithmetic-operation argument, not a bound on arbitrary-size integer bit operations.

scope: Selective independent execution and source/ownership review of three complete recorded answers. No listing was patched. Does not certify other rounds, all inputs, full peak memory, or whole-interview accuracy.
